counterevidence_considered.description: The only mechanism that could admit a repeated unit is the arm-pooling loop, which appends rows keyed by medium without deduplicating by vessel_id; the Counter check is diagnostic only and does not filter. However, since the supplied CSV contains no repeated vessel_id, no repeated entry actually occurs.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: no filtering by unit, but no duplicates exist in the input data

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue by searching for any vessel_id entering the row-independent Welch t-test more than once: I enumerated all 20 vessel_id values in data/input.csv (V01 through V20) and found each exactly once, with exactly 10 rows per medium arm; I traced the workflow to confirm every row contributes exactly one titer to exactly one arm list and that no join, resampling, or replicate expansion duplicates rows; and I cross-checked the reported arm means (5.000 and 5.700 g/L) and mean difference (0.700 g/L) against hand-computed values from the raw CSV, which matched, ruling out hidden duplication upstream of the reported statistics. No path by which an independent unit enters the procedure repeatedly could be constructed from the supplied files.
